1160	And it came to pass one day that, even so, one of
1161	the sons, who brought Father tefillin,
1162	it became clear at the last moment that they were Rabbeinu Tam's, and he took them off at the last moment because of Father's question.
1163	And indeed Father caught it at the last moment, did not recite the blessing, and they switched him to Rashi's before Rabbeinu Tam's.
1164	But there was a somewhat more inward case, which happened on one of the occasions
1165	when the son was already used to this question and answered automatically, "Yes, yes, it's Rashi," "Yes, yes, it's Rabbeinu Tam."
1166	A mistake came out, and Father recited the blessing over Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1167	And afterward: "Oh, what have I done?"
1168	The son came and apologized.
1169	Then came the words of comfort. It is written in the holy books that to every person it will happen
1170	once in his life that he will err and recite the blessing on Rabbeinu Tam's
1171	before Rashi's. Once in his life it will happen to him. So it is brought in the book Taamei HaMinhagim, where it is written:
1172	a tradition from holy men that the man who is careful all his days to put on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin and does not lack any of them
1173	all his days through any constraint, must be roused once to recite the blessings
1174	on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin and pray in them.
1175	He also brings there from the book Yakar Totefta, written by a kabbalist in the name of Rav Mordechai of Dubrovna,
1176	that Rabbeinu Tam arranged in the Heavenly court that whoever puts on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin will be roused at least once
1177	in his life to err and put on, with the blessing, Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin instead of Rashi's.
1178	And there is such a tradition in the name of the Holy Rav of Lublin, and afterward he brings further books and so on.
1179	In any case, for our purposes, even the mistake that happened with my father was done by deliberate providence
1180	from Heaven, because that is how it had to be, since Rabbeinu Tam requested in Heaven that whoever it may be,
1181	once will come to an error,
1182	so that he will get to recite the blessing and pray with Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1183	But our father was meticulous, very meticulous, between man and his fellow, between man
1184	and the Almighty, especially in monetary matters.
1185	For several years he would receive in the mail a calendar, the
1186	Or HaChaim calendar of Yeshivat Or HaChaim in Jerusalem. They would send it to him by mail every year.
1187	Right away our father would sit down, that very day he would sit and send them back
1188	an envelope with payment. Once we asked him:
1189	Why do they send it to you, and why do you pay what you never even asked for, and we already have a calendar
1190	at home? He answered that apparently I once donated to them,
1191	and since then they send to me regularly. Since they take the trouble to send, and even enclose an envelope
1192	for return payment, they are expecting to receive, so I do not change from what I did
1193	at the beginning, the first time. And so he continues to pay for the calendar although he owes them nothing; he did not ask
1194	that they send it to him again, but if they already send it and have grown used to it, then I too continue
1195	with what I did the first time. Caution in monetary matters, caution
1196	in his own monetary matters, on account of another's, yes?
1197	One who is careful in monetary matters is called a tzaddik. Noach, a righteous man.
1198	Our Sages tell us, the Gemara says, a tzaddik in money.
1199	As we produced a comprehensive shiur on the subject, called "Ish Tzaddik."
